messages:
dmitri: Quick midweek runway sanity check — seeing transient packet loss on the east-west interconnect since ~02:30 UTC. eu-west tail latency spiked, some inference requests fell back to larger variants. Can folks surface immediate impact to scheduled jobs and runway?

alice: Noted. Alerting graphs show packet_loss > 0.8% for interfaces between eu-west and us-central for the last 18m. Retries up ~210 req/min.

infra-bot: ALERT: network_interconnect_packet_loss exceeded threshold (0.5%) on eu-west <-> us-central 18m ago. Incident ID IN-2026-0421.

ben: Do we have concrete burn numbers? If retries + fallback are happening we could overshoot the weekly GPU-hours.

dmitri: Current quick calc: global forecasted GPU-hours this week = 18,500h. Measured burn so far = 11,400h after 3.5 days (projected week burn ~19,600h, +5.9%). eu-west specifically: planned 3,200h, actual+projected ~4,100h if retries continue (+28%). That's with fallback to larger model variants and failed cold starts.

carla: I'm on it — will try a focused drain & redeploy on a subset to force healthy routing; draining only burst pool hosts in eu-west for 10m to clear stuck KV caches.

carla: ```
# drain burst pool in eu-west (10m grace)
rila nodes drain --cluster=cluster-eu-west --pool=burst --grace=10m
# then trigger rolling deploy on serving-daemonset-eu
kubectl rollout restart ds/serving-daemonset-eu -n redwood-serving
```

alice: Logs from the routing plane show intermittent 5xxs with connection resets between proxies. I also see increased TCP retransmits on the ixp path. Might be a provider layer issue, not our software.

ben: If it's provider flakiness, moving committed reserved capacity won't help short-term. Two short options: 1) temporarily route EU non-critical traffic to us-central (latency hit, cheaper than scale-up) or 2) borrow 4 reserved nodes from us-central buffer to eu-west (cost + immediate runway headroom). Cost delta estimate: moving 4 nodes for 12h -> ~+3.6k GPU-hours/month prorated -> ~+$1.2k incremental this week; if we let user-facing errors persist, potential SLO penalties or failed jobs cost >> $12k in churn.

sasha: I'll open a short routing policy change canary: add rule prefer-region:false for non-low-latency routes and increase autoscaler headroom by +20% for eu-west only. If packet loss persists >30m we'll initiate borrowing.

dmitri: Agreed. Plan: 1) Carla drains and restarts 2) Sasha flips routing canary for non-critical routes (10% traffic) 3) Infra ops monitors burn and net metrics for 30m 4) If no improvement, move 4 nodes from us-central buffer to eu-west for 12h.

alice: Rolling metrics: after drain restart some 5xxs reduced. Packet loss still ~0.6% but retransmits down 30%. Keep monitoring.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE IN-2026-0421: packet_loss reduced to 0.45% after 12m; monitoring.

ben: If numbers hold, runway hit reduces to +8% vs +5.9% earlier projection — still above forecast but manageable without long-term changes. Recommend we not do full borrow yet.

carla: Drains completed on 4 hosts (burst pool). Redeploy rolled. Observed KV warmup; cold starts dropped ~42% for affected pods.

sasha: Canary applied. 10% of non-critical EU traffic now routed off-region. No increased user complaints in the first 12m.

dmitri: OK — hold on borrow for now. Action items: Carla keep watch for 2h, Sasha keep canary for 1h and report, Alice autoscaling alert thresholds to remain at +20% headroom until EOW if stable. Re-evaluate in next runway check.

carla: ack :thumbsup:

ben: ack — will update the weekly capacity sheet with new projected burn +8% and note the network incident cause.

infra-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: IN-2026-0421 -> packet_loss returned to baseline. Closure in 4h if no regressions.
